learning_objective: 🎯 Welcome to the digital age! Discover how the internet and outsourcing have completely transformed how businesses operate today.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: E-business means conducting industry, trade, and commerce using computer networks (the Internet). It is broader than E-commerce, which only focuses on buying and selling online.

1. B2B (Business to Business, e.g., a car maker buying tires online). 2. B2C (Business to Customer, e.g., you buying shoes on Amazon). 3. C2C (Customer to Customer, e.g., selling your old books on OLX). 4. Intra-B (within the same business).
Contracting out non-core activities (like customer care, payroll, or cleaning) to specialized outside agencies so the business can focus on its main core activities (like product design).
Online business comes with risks like transaction risks (default on delivery or payment), data storage risks (hacking, viruses), and intellectual property risks.

fun_activity.title: 🛒 The E-Biz Labeler
fun_activity.instructions: Open your phone. Amazon/Flipkart = B2C. OLX/Quikr = C2C. A customer care number you call = Probably a BPO (Outsourcing). You are actively participating in emerging modes of business every single day!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate clearly between E-Business (broader, includes production, inventory, HR) and E-Commerce (narrower, only buying/selling).
📌 C2C commerce is highly tested; always give the example of OLX or eBay for selling second-hand goods.
📌 Why do companies outsource? (Core Competence, Cost Reduction, Quest for Excellence).
quick_recap: ⭐ E-business breaks geographical boundaries and allows 24/7/365 operations.
⭐ Lack of personal touch and security concerns are major limitations of e-business.
⭐ KPO (Knowledge Process Outsourcing) involves highly skilled, knowledge-based tasks like R&D or legal services, unlike BPO which handles routine tasks.
